title.en: Historical reference versus fictional invention boundary

summary: Keep sourced reconstruction, informed interpretation and free invention visibly separate while allowing fictional scenes to remix broad craft and age cues.
objective: Every externally presented historical or cultural assertion points to reviewed evidence and uncertainty, while invented forms, labels and stories are clearly described as fiction.
applies_when: A fictional or interpretive scene uses real-world reference images, collection objects, period cues, place names, scripts, dress or ritual forms.
intent_signals: separate museum evidence from invented scene dressing
label which old-town details are fictional
example_prompts: Create an invented port workshop inspired by broad repair and material cues, with no claim that its machinery reconstructs a real place.
Build an interpretive gallery room where sourced object facts and fictional connective scenes use different labels.
negative_signals: mix living cultural symbols as generic decoration
copy reference asset without rights review
not_for: Replacing historians, culture bearers, curators or rights holders when a project makes specific public claims.
Using this creative record as evidence for dates, provenance, construction, dress, language, ritual or technology.

principles: Classify each consequential element as sourced reconstruction, evidence-bounded interpretation or free invention before describing it publicly.
Visual plausibility and repeated online imagery are not evidence. Specific claims about a people, place, object, event or period need reviewed sources and uncertainty appropriate to the claim.
As an authored project policy, track factual support and reproduction permission in separate review fields; do not approve redistribution from citation alone.

Avoid token motifs that stand in for a whole living culture. When cultural specificity matters, involve appropriate expertise and preserve names, context and disagreement rather than blending markers into generic atmosphere.
Fiction remains flexible when it says what is invented. Broad age, repair, craft and material cues can be remixed without attaching unsupported real-world attribution.
implementation: Maintain a reference ledger outside the mesh with element ID, intended claim, source locator, rights status, interpretation note, reviewer and unresolved uncertainty. Leave entries explicitly invented when no factual claim is intended.
In Blender, assign stable semantic IDs and evidence-class metadata to claim-bearing objects or parts. Keep reference images and source notes out of redistribution unless rights permit them.

For the fictional port workshop, invent names and machinery while using repair, support and material-age cues as creative grammar; label it fictional. For the interpretive gallery, isolate sourced objects from invented transitions and scenery.

Export only the metadata needed for presentation, such as claim class, public label key and source-record key. Project review must not approve redistribution or source fidelity from the presence of a glTF extras field alone.

In Three.js, render sourced facts, bounded interpretations and fictional connective text with distinct labels available in the accessible companion interface; link claim-bearing items to the reviewed source record where publication allows.
When evidence changes, update the ledger and affected labels as one content revision. Reset changes interaction state, not provenance or claim classification.
observable_checks: Audit every specific date, place, named culture, historical function or reconstruction statement; each has a source record and uncertainty or is rewritten as fiction.
Inspect a sourced object, an interpretive reconstruction and an invented prop; their public labels clearly distinguish the three classes without relying on color alone.
Trace a visible claim-bearing element through Blender semantic ID, exported metadata, runtime object and companion source entry.
Review reference images, scans, typefaces and copied assets separately for allowed use; no factual citation is presented as permission.
Remove unreviewed cultural markers and named attributions; the fictional composition still works through spatial, functional and material choices.
Revise one evidence entry and verify every affected runtime label changes together while saved interaction state and unrelated fiction remain stable.

creative_affordances: Create alternate fictional histories or composite places when the brief invites them, using clear invented labels rather than counterfeit provenance.
Show uncertainty as multiple interpretive variants, layered reconstruction states or curator notes when the evidence genuinely supports more than one reading.
known_limits: Authored workflow guidance with no historical, cultural, legal or rights determination for any specific project.
This record supplies no factual claims or sources; each real-world assertion requires its own evidence and review.
